Xmarine for iPhone and iPad

Connect an NMEA3WiFi gateway, check your instrument readings, and learn the cockpit controls.

Gateway setup · Connect Xmarine · Cockpit · Autopilot

1. Set up the NMEA3WiFi gateway

  1. Join the gateway’s own Wi‑Fi from your iPhone or iPad. If the factory settings are unchanged, the network is NMEA3WIFI and its password is 12345678.
  2. Open http://192.168.4.1 while still connected to the gateway.
  3. Under EXTERNAL NETWORK, enter your boat router’s Wi‑Fi name and password. For automatic addressing, enter 0 in the IP field. If you use a fixed address, choose an unused address on your boat’s network.
  4. Under WIFI PORTS SETTINGS, set the TCP port to 10110 for this example. Select P1>TCP and/or P2>TCP for the wired inputs you actually use. If your instrument readings come from SeaTalk1, enable ST>TCP.
  5. Select ALSO CONNECT TO EXTERNAL and save. Once connected, note the gateway’s external IP shown near the firmware version. Switch your iPhone or iPad to the boat router’s Wi‑Fi.

Vela Navega’s NMEA3WiFi settings reference

2. Connect Xmarine

  1. Open Settings → Network → Boat WiFi in Xmarine.
  2. Enter the gateway’s external IP and the matching TCP port. Use 10110 if you followed the example above.
  3. Tap Use Boat WiFi. Return to the cockpit and look for live readings. If they stay blank, open Network → Raw data and check the phone’s Wi‑Fi, gateway address, TCP port, and routing.

3. Use the cockpit

HDG is heading, COG is course over ground, SOG is speed over ground, and AWA/AWS are apparent wind angle and speed. A dash means that reading has yet to arrive.

Drag or pinch to move or zoom the map. Tap N UP to change orientation. Use the map controls for routes and measuring. GRIB wind forecasts require internet access. To move the data bars, hold the gear icon for more than two seconds, drag the instruments, and tap Done.

4. Set up and use the autopilot

Autopilot control requires compatible bidirectional SeaTalk1 equipment. The TCP connection above carries instrument readings. Xmarine sends pilot commands over UDP.

  1. In the gateway’s Wi‑Fi settings, enable a UDP port and UDP>ST. Match the gateway address and UDP port in Xmarine’s network settings. The gateway’s factory UDP port is 2000 if unchanged.
  2. In the cockpit, tap PILOT, read and accept the prompt, then use the pilot controls. Check the state on the physical autopilot control head.

Stay aboard, keep watch, and be ready to take the helm using the boat’s controls. Use the vessel’s primary navigation and steering equipment.
